quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A yellow triangular sign with black letters means no passing zone. You will see it on the left side of a two-lane road where you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: How much space should you leave between your car and the car ahead?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three to six seconds
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, leave three to six seconds of space between your car and the car ahead. Increase this distance when driving faster.

questions.question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as cars on your right and left. What should you do?

options.text: Yield to the car on your left.
Yield to the car on your right.
Wait until all cars leave before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the car on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the car on your right has the right-of-way. Let that car go first.

questions.question: The light is green, but cars are blocking the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Do not enter the intersection until traffic moves.
Follow the other cars and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until traffic moves.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection if cars are blocking it. If you get stuck in the intersection when the light turns red, you will block cross traffic and can get a ticket.

questions.question: Cars are passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway. What should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On a road with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. On an interstate, use the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic.

questions.question: You are turning left at an intersection. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Pedestrians waiting on the sidewalk for a walk signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All cars coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicycles, and all vehicles moving toward you on their green light.

questions.question: What must bicyclists do?

options.text: Follow the same traffic laws as car drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the same traffic laws as car drivers.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists must obey the same traffic laws as drivers. The same right-of-way rules apply to both.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black marks warn you about hazards. Round signs warn only about railroad crossings.

questions.question: How can you make room for cars entering the freeway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane.
questions.explanation: When cars are entering the freeway, change lanes if you can to create a gap. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to let them enter safely.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to go through a red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection.
questions.explanation: Follow a police officer's directions instead of traffic lights and signs. Their instructions override traffic signals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Parking for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for people with disability plates or placards only.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: A yellow left turn arrow means the protected turn is ending and oncoming traffic is coming. Prepare to yield.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: You can pass on the right if the way is clear.
You can pass on the left if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left if the way is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass on the left if no traffic is coming. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: Cars are merging from an on-ramp on your right on the interstate. What should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: When cars are merging from the right, move to the left lane if you can. This gives them space to enter safely.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: You can pass on the right if the way is clear.
You can pass on the left if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left if the way is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross it to pass on the left if the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you while driving.
Keep your eyes moving to scan for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to scan for hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for possible hazards. Looking only at the road directly in front of you is dangerous. Scan ahead and stay alert to vehicles around you.

questions.question: You must tell the MVD about an address change within:
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 days.
questions.explanation: You must notify the MVD about any change to your name or address within 10 days.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
On the left side of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, start in the lane closest to the centerline. Begin your turn just before you reach the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first legal lane available.

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, you should:

options.text: Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign means you are near a school. Watch for children and stop if they are in the crosswalk.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus picking up or dropping off children, you must come to a complete stop before reaching the bus. This applies no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: If you parallel park facing downhill:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the curb or side of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the curb or side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the curb or side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and drive with a blood alcohol level of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol in drivers under 21. Any trace of alcohol in your system will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: There are two traffic lanes going your direction. You are in the left lane and many vehicles are passing you on the right. If the driver behind you wants to go faster, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic flows smoothly.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for faster driving, passing, and turning left. Use the right lane when driving slower than traffic around you, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay aware of what is happening around your vehicle at all times. Watch the front, sides, and rear. This helps you spot problems and adjust your speed or position.

questions.question: If you want to enter the freeway but don't see a gap in traffic, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: If you don't see a gap in traffic, slow down on the ramp and wait. Do not stop at the end of the ramp. You need room to speed up and match traffic before entering the freeway.

questions.question: You must yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights by:

options.text: Driving to the right edge of the road as far as possible and stopping.
Moving to the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.
Stopping immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving to the right edge of the road as far as possible and stopping.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using a siren and flashing lights by driving to the right edge and stopping. Do not stop in an intersection. You can drive again after the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When driving in fog or mist, do not use high beam headlights because:

options.text: The light will bounce back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will bounce back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect back into your eyes. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter traffic by crossing a sidewalk, you should:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot, stop before crossing the sidewalk. Pedestrians and traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Alcohol is:
questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slow.

questions.question: When driving at night and approaching a car from behind, switch to low beam headlights when you are within:
questions.correctAnswerText: 200 feet.
questions.explanation: At night, switch from high beam to low beam headlights when you are within 200 feet of a vehicle ahead.
